items.why: The report puts the 248-250 cm-1 maximum at 1.8703 eV and lists a second high area (244 at 1.8999 eV), but it never names a double incoming/outgoing resonance or the A2s exciton; the summary says only that the peak 'falls by more than 30x by 1.94 eV'.
It gives the resonance at '1.8703 eV (+130 meV above A1s)' but does not assign it to the A2s, saying only that PLE 'would turn the 1.870 eV ... resonances into exciton assignments'.
The report says the 480-510 group is 'present in 8 of 9 spectra' and does not describe it appearing only at the A2s incoming resonance, vanishing just above it, then reappearing about 26 meV higher.
It reports strong growth near 1.93 eV and resolves a doublet at 492.7/495.9 cm-1, but it finds two peaks, not three, and explicitly denies dispersion: 'not as a dispersive or strain-like shift'.
The report rejects dispersion and does not infer dark excitonic states with minima or saddle points in their dispersion.
It notes the parallel-minus-crossed subtraction 'removes most of the E' intensity', but it does not say that residual background or negative values are processing artifacts.
It states 'The 495 group has no assignment in the notes I read' and that the overtone or combination ideas 'are arithmetic hypotheses, not verified'.

wrong_claims.why: It denies dispersion, but it does not assert the feature is a 2A1' overtone; it lists '2 x 248 = 496' only as an unverified hypothesis.
It does not attribute the 495 cm-1 feature to Si or hBN; Si is discussed only for the 520 cm-1 calibration line.
